TaskName: [DAILY][ALL] Confirm EPM service availability and daily maintenance
Description: Confirms every production EPM service is reachable through SSO and that the Oracle daily maintenance completed and produced a current Artifact Snapshot, so users can work and a recovery point exists. FSSG: Performs the check, manages incidents and Oracle SRs. Finance: None (informed of outages).
Instruction: Steps: 1) Sign in to each production service (FCCS, ARCS, EDMCS, Planning, Narrative Reporting) through the corporate SSO URL and confirm the home page loads. 2) Check the Oracle Cloud status page and service announcements for unplanned outages or maintenance notices affecting the services. 3) In each service, confirm the daily maintenance completed: check the Artifact Snapshot timestamp (Migration > Snapshots) or the Activity Report and confirm it is within the last 24 hours. 4) Confirm the daily maintenance start time still matches the approved window in the Environment Configuration Register. 5) Record the result per service in the task comments. Expected result: All five services available through SSO; an Artifact Snapshot dated within the last 24 hours exists for each; maintenance windows unchanged. Evidence: Per service: sign-in time, Artifact Snapshot date/time (screenshot or Activity Report reference); incident/SR number for any exception. If not successful: Service unavailable: raise a P1 incident, check the Oracle status page, open an Oracle SR for a production outage and notify the FSSG Lead and the Finance close lead immediately. Snapshot missing or failed: raise a P2 incident and Oracle SR, and postpone administrative changes (metadata imports, restructures, deployments) until a valid backup is confirmed. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Were all five production EPM services available through SSO and did each produce an Artifact Snapshot within the last 24 hours?

TaskName: [DAILY][ALL] Review overnight scheduled jobs and next-24-hour schedule
Description: Detects failed, cancelled, long-running or missed scheduled jobs and confirms that jobs due in the next 24 hours are scheduled correctly. FSSG: Performs the review, re-runs per runbook, raises incidents. Finance: None (informed of close-critical failures).
Instruction: Steps: 1) Open the Jobs console in FCCS, Planning and ARCS and the job/history views in EDMCS and Narrative Reporting; filter to the period since the last check. 2) Compare executed jobs with the Job Schedule Register. Identify jobs with status Error, Warning or Cancelled, jobs still running beyond their expected duration, and expected jobs that did not run. 3) For each failed integration job open Data Integration Process Details and capture the process ID and log. 4) Review the scheduled jobs list in each service and confirm that jobs due in the next 24 hours exist, are active, and have the correct time and time zone. 5) Log an incident for every exception not already tracked and link existing incidents. Expected result: All expected jobs completed with Success; none missing; jobs due in the next 24 hours scheduled correctly; every exception linked to an incident. Evidence: For each exception: job name, job/process ID, status, start and end time, incident number; note confirming reconciliation against the Job Schedule Register. If not successful: Re-run a failed job only if the runbook allows a re-run and the cause is understood (for example a transient connection error); otherwise raise an incident and notify the job owner. Close-critical job failures during the close window are P2 and the Finance close lead is notified. A missing or disabled schedule is restored from the Job Schedule Register under the approved change process. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Did all expected overnight scheduled jobs complete successfully, with no missing or disabled jobs due in the next 24 hours?

TaskName: [DAILY][GB] Verify GB to EPM pipeline execution and load completeness
Description: Confirms GB data reached the EPM applications completely and without unresolved rejections, so Finance works with current data. FSSG: Verifies technical completeness, fixes technical causes, re-runs loads. Finance: Approves mapping changes; validates loaded balances.
Instruction: Steps: 1) Confirm the GB source extract for the business date was delivered (file or interface delivery confirmation defined for the GB interface). 2) In Data Integration open Process Details for the GB pipeline/integrations and confirm each scheduled run ended with Success. 3) For each integration compare records extracted with records imported and loaded to the target; record counts and, where available, control totals. 4) Review the process log and Workbench for rejected rows, unmapped members and validation errors. 5) Record the results and raise incidents for exceptions. Expected result: All scheduled GB runs succeeded; source and loaded record counts reconcile (or the difference is explained by approved filters); no unresolved rejected or unmapped records. Evidence: Pipeline/integration name, process ID, status, timestamps, source vs loaded record counts, rejected record count, log extract for exceptions, incident numbers. If not successful: Source file missing or late: contact the GB interface owner and raise an incident. Load failure: review the log, correct the technical cause and re-run per runbook. Unmapped members: notify the mapping/data owner; FSSG does not create or change mappings without an approved request. Partial load during the close window: P2 and notify the Finance close lead. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Did all scheduled GB pipeline runs complete successfully with reconciled record counts and no unresolved rejected or unmapped records?

Evidence: Integration name, process ID, status, period, timestamps, source vs loaded record counts, rejected record count, incident numbers. Load failure: correct the technical cause and re-run per runbook. Unmapped members: notify the mapping/data owner. Close-window impact: P2 and notify the Finance close lead. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Did all scheduled Oracle EBS pipeline runs complete successfully with reconciled record counts and no unresolved rejected or unmapped records?

TaskName: [DAILY][FX] Verify daily FX rate load against the approved source
Description: Confirms daily FX rates are complete and identical to the approved source, preventing translation errors. Applies only if daily rates are loaded; otherwise set Active = No. FSSG: Loads and technically compares rates with the approved source. Finance: Owns the rate source and values; approves any exception.
Instruction: Steps: 1) Obtain the approved daily FX rate source for the business date as defined in the Environment Configuration Register. 2) Confirm the FX rate load job/integration ended with Success; record the process ID. 3) Confirm every currency pair in the Currency Pair Register is loaded for the correct date or period, rate type and scenario, with no blank or zero rates. 4) Compare loaded rates with the approved source for all pairs (preferred: exported rates vs source file). Rates must match to the precision of the source. 5) Record expected, loaded and matched pair counts and any differences. Expected result: Load succeeded; 100% of expected pairs present; all loaded rates match the approved source. Evidence: Source file name and timestamp, load process ID and status, comparison output (pairs expected/loaded/matched), list of differences, incident numbers. If not successful: Source missing: contact the Treasury/rate source owner; do not key rates manually unless Finance provides approved rates in writing. Mismatch or missing pairs: correct the cause, reload from the approved source and notify the Finance rate owner. FSSG never approves rate values. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Were all expected daily FX rates loaded successfully and do they match the approved source for every currency pair?

TaskName: [DAILY][FCCS] Verify FCCS loads and scheduled consolidation jobs
Description: Confirms FCCS-specific loads and any scheduled consolidation, translation and business rule jobs ran without technical errors and within expected duration. Source pipeline health is covered by FSSG_D003/FSSG_D004 and is not repeated here. FSSG: Monitors job health and investigates technical failures. Finance: Runs or approves consolidations; validates consolidated results and data status.
Instruction: Steps: 1) Review FCCS-only scheduled loads listed in the Job Schedule Register and confirm Success. 2) In the Jobs console review scheduled Consolidation, Translation, business rule and Refresh Database jobs: status, errors/warnings and duration against the baseline. 3) For failures capture the job log and check for metadata or rule changes in the last 24 hours (EDMCS synchronization, deployments). 4) Note entities left Impacted by a failed job and pass the list to Finance for information (FSSG does not judge business results). Expected result: All FCCS scheduled loads and consolidation-related jobs succeeded within expected duration. Evidence: Job names, job IDs, status, duration, log extract for failures, incident numbers. If not successful: Raise an incident with the job log. During the close window do not re-run consolidation without agreement from the Finance close lead, because a re-run changes data status. Significant performance degradation: incident and Oracle SR with the Activity Report. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Did all FCCS scheduled data loads and consolidation-related jobs complete successfully within their expected duration?

TaskName: [DAILY][ARCS] Verify ARCS data imports and matching jobs
Description: Confirms balance and transaction data needed by preparers was imported and that scheduled matching jobs ran without technical errors. FSSG: Monitors imports and matching job health. Finance: Prepares, reviews and signs off reconciliations; resolves unmatched items; owns profiles.
Instruction: Steps: 1) In the ARCS Jobs view review scheduled balance imports (Reconciliation Compliance) and, if Transaction Matching is used, transaction loads and auto-match runs. 2) Confirm each job ended with Success and processed the expected period. 3) Review import logs for rejected records and records not assigned to a reconciliation profile. 4) Record results; raise incidents for technical failures. Expected result: All scheduled ARCS imports and matching jobs succeeded; no unresolved rejected records. Evidence: Job names, job IDs, status, period, rejected record counts, incident numbers. If not successful: Technical failure: correct the cause and re-run per runbook, raise an incident. Records without a profile or unmatched business items are passed to the Finance reconciliation owner; FSSG does not change profiles or match transactions. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Did all scheduled ARCS data imports and matching jobs complete successfully with no unresolved rejected records?

TaskName: [DAILY][EDMCS] Verify EDMCS request, subscription and export processing
Description: Detects technical failures in metadata requests, subscriptions and exports before they cause metadata gaps in target applications. FSSG: Monitors processing and target imports; fixes technical causes. Finance: Data owners raise and approve metadata requests.
Instruction: Steps: 1) Review requests with failed validations or stuck in processing; report requests waiting on approval beyond the agreed time to the data owners (information only). 2) Review subscription requests generated in the last 24 hours and any subscription errors. 3) Review scheduled exports/extracts and the related metadata import jobs in the target applications (FCCS, Planning, ARCS) for errors. 4) Record results; raise incidents for technical failures. Expected result: No technical failures in requests, subscriptions, exports or target metadata imports; pending approvals reported to data owners. Evidence: Request IDs, subscription/export job references, target import job IDs, incident numbers. If not successful: Technical error: capture the validation/export message, correct the technical cause and re-run, raise an incident. Business validation failures go back to the requester or data owner; FSSG does not approve metadata requests. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Were all EDMCS requests, subscriptions and scheduled exports processed without technical errors in the last 24 hours?

TaskName: [DAILY][Planning] Verify Planning data loads, business rules and data maps
Description: Confirms scheduled Planning loads, calculations and data movements ran without technical errors, so planners see current data. FSSG: Monitors job health; re-runs per runbook. Finance: FP&A validates plan/forecast results.
Instruction: Steps: 1) Review the Planning Jobs console for scheduled data loads, business rules/rulesets, data maps/Smart Push and Refresh Database jobs. 2) Confirm each job ended with Success and within expected duration. 3) For data loads review rejected records; for rules review error messages in the job log. 4) Record results; raise incidents for failures. Expected result: All scheduled Planning jobs succeeded within expected duration with no rejected records. Evidence: Job names, job IDs, status, duration, rejected record counts, incident numbers. If not successful: Correct the technical cause and re-run per runbook; raise an incident. Do not re-run calculations that overwrite planner data without agreement from the FP&A owner. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Did all scheduled Planning data loads, business rules and data maps complete successfully?

TaskName: [DAILY][Narrative Reporting] Verify scheduled report refresh and distribution jobs
Description: Detects failed scheduled report refreshes or distributions. Applies only where daily Narrative Reporting jobs are configured; otherwise set Active = No. FSSG: Monitors technical refresh and distribution. Finance: Report owners approve content and distribution.
Instruction: Steps: 1) Review scheduled report refresh, bursting and distribution jobs in Narrative Reporting. 2) Confirm each job ended successfully and the data source connections (FCCS, Planning) responded. 3) Record results; raise incidents for failures. Expected result: All scheduled refresh and distribution jobs succeeded. Evidence: Job/report names, status, timestamps, incident numbers. If not successful: Data source connection error: check the connection and credentials (see FSSG_M003) and raise an incident. Do not re-distribute reports without the report owner's approval. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Did all scheduled Narrative Reporting refresh and distribution jobs for the day complete successfully?

TaskName: [DAILY][ALL] Review SSO, provisioning and access incidents
Description: Ensures authentication, provisioning and authorization issues are triaged quickly and that every access change is backed by an approved request. FSSG: Triages incidents; executes approved access changes. Finance: Application owners approve access requests.
Instruction: Steps: 1) Review new incidents and requests for SSO/authentication failures, missing roles or groups and access-denied errors across the five services. 2) For SSO failures check whether multiple users are affected; a pattern indicates an identity provider or certificate issue and is escalated as P1/P2. 3) For each provisioning change confirm an approved access request exists before execution and that group synchronization from the identity provider completed. 4) Confirm any emergency or temporary access granted is time-bound and recorded. Expected result: All new access incidents triaged; no access change without approval; widespread SSO issues escalated. Evidence: Incident/request numbers, approval references, affected users count for SSO patterns. If not successful: Widespread SSO failure: P1/P2, engage the identity provider team and Oracle SR if the EPM identity domain is affected. Access change without approval: do not execute; return to the requester. Unauthorized access found: revoke per security procedure and inform the application owner and IT Security. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Have all new SSO, provisioning and access incidents been triaged, with every access change executed against an approved request?

TaskName: [DAILY][ALL] Review open incidents and Oracle SRs and issue daily status
Description: Keeps open incidents and Oracle SRs moving and gives Finance one daily view of EPM operational health. FSSG: Owns incident follow-up and the daily status. Finance: Receives the status.
Instruction: Steps: 1) Review open EPM incidents and Oracle SRs: severity, owner, age and next action; escalate overdue items per the escalation matrix. 2) Update Oracle SRs that are waiting on FSSG. 3) Issue the daily status (services, jobs, pipelines, FX, open P1/P2 items) to the FSSG Lead and the agreed Finance distribution list. 4) Hand over open items to the next shift where applicable. Expected result: All open items reviewed; overdue items escalated; daily status issued. Evidence: Daily status message or report reference; list of escalated items. If not successful: Unowned or overdue P1/P2 item: escalate to the FSSG Lead the same day. A No answer does not by itself block completion: record the incident/SR number, the exception and the agreed next step in the task comments and attach the evidence before submitting.
QText1: Has the daily EPM operations status been issued with all open incidents and Oracle SRs reviewed for ageing and escalation?
